result.title: BEARING: Who Is Talking to Whom? Grounding Acoustic Direction in Vision for Online Multi-Party Conversation
result.comment: 26 pages, 15 figures, 16 tables. Includes supplementary material. Demo video as an ancillary file
result.summary: Understanding a group conversation means deciding, from video and audio, who is speaking and to whom. Leading systems treat these tasks offline on single-channel clips and align models with a self-evaluation reward. We propose BEARING, a geometry-first alternative built on one measured signal: the direction from which a microphone array beside the camera hears a sound. A label-free calibration learned from the stream registers this direction into the camera image, and an online registry of faces, voices and directions needs no enrollment. The registered direction serves as (i) a visual prompt for a vision-language model, a marker on the speaker or an arrow toward an off-screen source; (ii) one input of a reliability-weighted fusion with visual active-speaker detection, for speakers in the same direction from the array; and (iii) a verifiable reward for alignment: the named speaker must sit where the sound comes from, the confidence must match that check, and always answering "group" earns nothing. Every decision is online, with the lookahead as an explicit parameter. On 9,498 addressee-labelled utterances from three AMI sites and egocentric EasyCom, the direction prompt raises speaker accuracy from 54% to 74%; addressee accuracy moves by about two points, because telling one addressee from the group depends on the words more than on where people are. For co-located speakers on AVDIAR, visual active-speaker detection holds 95% where direction alone falls to 59%. The verifiable reward beats self-evaluation under GRPO, reward-ranked fine-tuning and DPO; shrinking the lookahead from 5 s to 0.5 s costs 4.5 DER points on AMI, and learning the registration online costs a dip in the first two minutes before the system overtakes vision alone. Code and evaluation protocols will be released.

AI.brief_summary: BEARING 把麦克风阵列测得的声音方向当作几何信号，在线无标签校准后注册到相机图像，作为视觉提示注入 VLM，并与视觉主动说话人检测做可靠性加权融合，还用方向一致性构造可验证奖励来训练说话人/受话人判断。
AI.relevance_reason: 几何线索作为提示注入 VLM、以及「可验证奖励替代自评」可供核查视觉证据如何进入判断与监督如何分配，显式 lookahead 参数也对应动态计算与停止决策；但任务是多人对话受话人识别，未涉及 latent 推理状态，迁移需自行判断。
